literature.headline_zh: 人偏肺病毒近期研究:病毒学机制、心血管风险与儿童重症预测同步推进。
literature.lead_zh: 本周文献聚焦人偏肺病毒(HMPV)的病毒组装机制、抗病毒候选物、心血管并发症负担、儿童重症预测工具以及疫情后病原体生态演变,呈现基础研究与临床证据的同步更新。
key_findings_zh: 采用靶向基质蛋白M的反义PPMO可使M蛋白减少超95%,病毒滴度显著下降,并阻断病毒核糖核蛋白向质膜组装位点的定位,为抗HMPV药物设计提供新靶点 [10.1128/jvi.01066-26]。
系统综述显示HMPV住院患者既存心血管疾病比例达10%–80%,急性心血管事件发生率5%–25%,心衰加重最常见,提示重症与死亡风险升高 [10.1016/j.jinf.2026.106843]。
研究者通过计算筛选鉴定出M294与C11两种植物成分,可同时抑制甲型流感神经氨酸酶和HMPV融合蛋白,被视为广谱抗病毒候选先导分子 [10.1371/journal.pone.0348517]。
基于540例单纯HMPV感染患儿的回顾性研究构建列线图模型,纳入中性粒细胞、淋巴细胞、前白蛋白及肺部啰音等6项指标,AUC为0.743,可实现早期重症风险分层 [10.3390/children13091177]。
沙特三级中心八年监测显示,HMPV占总检测数的3.6%,主要影响0–5岁儿童,且疫情后阳性病原谱显著多样化 [10.3390/pathogens15090918]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 疫情后呼吸道病毒生态重塑持续,多地区观察到HMPV呈现新的季节性高峰与基因型(B2为主)优势;缺乏特效疗法使高危人群心血管并发症和重症负担突出,亟需针对性药物与监测策略。
literature.caveats_zh: 部分结论基于计算模拟或单中心便利调查,仍需体外与前瞻性验证。
literature.headline_en: HMPV Weekly Brief: Assembly Mechanism, Cardiovascular Risk, and Pediatric Severity Tools.
literature.lead_en: Recent HMPV literature advances concurrently on virologic mechanisms, broad-spectrum antiviral candidates, cardiovascular burden, pediatric severity prediction, and post-pandemic ecological shifts, bridging basic and clinical evidence.
key_findings_en: An antisense PPMO targeting the M protein achieved >95% reduction in M expression, significantly lowering viral titers and blocking vRNP localization to plasma-membrane assembly sites, offering a potential antiviral target [10.1128/jvi.01066-26].

A PRISMA systematic review found 10%–80% of hospitalized HMPV patients had pre-existing cardiovascular disease and 5%–25% experienced acute cardiovascular events, with heart failure exacerbation most common and higher ICU admission and mortality [10.1016/j.jinf.2026.106843].

Computational screening identified phytoconstituents M294 and C11 as dual inhibitors of influenza A neuraminidase and HMPV fusion protein, positioned as broad-spectrum antiviral leads pending experimental confirmation [10.1371/journal.pone.0348517].

A retrospective nomogram from 540 children with isolated HMPV infection incorporated neutrophil count, lymphocyte count, prealbumin, crackles, wheezes, and sex, achieving AUC 0.743 for stratifying severe respiratory illness risk [10.3390/children13091177].

An eight-year Saudi tertiary-center study documented HMPV at 3.6% of respiratory viral detections, predominantly in children aged 0–5, with notable post-restriction diversification of circulating respiratory viruses [10.3390/pathogens15090918].
literature.trend_or_risk_en: Post-pandemic respiratory virus ecology continues to reshape, with HMPV showing altered seasonality and B2 lineage dominance in some regions; absent specific therapies leave vulnerable groups at risk of cardiovascular complications and severe disease, underscoring the need for targeted surveillance and drug development.
literature.caveats_en: Several leads rely on computational predictions or single-center convenience samples and require in vitro and prospective clinical validation.
literature.brief_en: This week’s HMPV literature covers five threads: (1) mechanistic work showing M-protein knockdown disrupts vRNP membrane localization and reduces titers; (2) a systematic review quantifying cardiovascular comorbidity and acute events in adult HMPV hospitalizations; (3) in silico identification of broad-spectrum phytoconstituent inhibitors against influenza NA and HMPV F protein; (4) a validated pediatric nomogram for early severe-illness risk stratification in isolated HMPV infection; and (5) surveillance evidence of post-restriction ecological shifts, with HMPV concentrated in young children and B2 lineage predominance. The convergence of mechanistic, clinical, and epidemiologic signals highlights an urgent need for HMPV-specific antivirals, vaccines, and structured surveillance.

literature.zh: 本周文献聚焦人偏肺病毒(HMPV)的病毒组装机制、抗病毒候选物、心血管并发症负担、儿童重症预测工具以及疫情后病原体生态演变,呈现基础研究与临床证据的同步更新。；采用靶向基质蛋白M的反义PPMO可使M蛋白减少超95%,病毒滴度显著下降,并阻断病毒核糖核蛋白向质膜组装位点的定位,为抗HMPV药物设计提供新靶点 [10.1128/jvi.01066-26]。；系统综述显示HMPV住院患者既存心血管疾病比例达10%–80%,急性心血管事件发生率5%–25%,心衰加重最常见,提示重症与死亡风险升高 [10.1016/j.jinf.2026.106843]。；研究者通过计算筛选鉴定出M294与C11两种植物成分,可同时抑制甲型流感神经氨酸酶和HMPV融合蛋白,被视为广谱抗病毒候选先导分子 [10.1371/journal.pone.0348517]。；基于540例单纯HMPV感染患儿的回顾性研究构建列线图模型,纳入中性粒细胞、淋巴细胞、前白蛋白及肺部啰音等6项指标,AUC为0.743,可实现早期重症风险分层 [10.3390/children13091177]。
literature.en: Recent HMPV literature advances concurrently on virologic mechanisms, broad-spectrum antiviral candidates, cardiovascular burden, pediatric severity prediction, and post-pandemic ecological shifts, bridging basic and clinical evidence. An antisense PPMO targeting the M protein achieved >95% reduction in M expression, significantly lowering viral titers and blocking vRNP localization to plasma-membrane assembly sites, offering a potential antiviral target [10.1128/jvi.01066-26]. A PRISMA systematic review found 10%–80% of hospitalized HMPV patients had pre-existing cardiovascular disease and 5%–25% experienced acute cardiovascular events, with heart failure exacerbation most common and higher ICU admission and mortality [10.1016/j.jinf.2026.106843]. Computational screening identified phytoconstituents M294 and C11 as dual inhibitors of influenza A neuraminidase and HMPV fusion protein, positioned as broad-spectrum antiviral leads pending experimental confirmation [10.1371/journal.pone.0348517]. A retrospective nomogram from 540 children with isolated HMPV infection incorporated neutrophil count, lymphocyte count, prealbumin, crackles, wheezes, and sex, achieving AUC 0.743 for stratifying severe respiratory illness risk [10.3390/children13091177].

papers.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes and Acute Human Metapneumovirus Infection in Adults: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute respiratory viral infections, including influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2, are well-recognized as being associated with cardiovascular events (CVEs). In contrast, the cardiovascular impact of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) remains poorly characterized. We aimed to describe the prevalence of pre-existing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and the incidence of acute CVEs in adults with laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection. METHODS: PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar (Jan.-2000/Sept.-2025). Observational studies and clinical trials reporting pre-existing CVDs and/or CVEs in adults (≥18 years) were included. RESULTS: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria, of which nine underwent critical appraisal. Most involved hospitalized older adults. Pre-existing CVD was reported in 10%-80% of HMPV-infected patients, with chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease being the most common conditions. Acute CVEs, particularly heart failure exacerbations, occurred in 5%-25% of hospitalized patients. Underlying CVD was consistently linked to increased severity of HMPV illness, including higher rates of ICU admission and mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Acute HMPV infection frequently occurs in adults with pre-existing CVD and may be associated with CVEs in older hospitalized populations. However, evidence remains limited and largely observational. These findings highlight the need to increase awareness of the potential CV complications associated with HMPV infection. TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO [CRD420251164583].

analysis.summary_en: This systematic literature review explores the cardiovascular impact of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection in adults. While acute respiratory viral infections like influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 are well-documented for their association with cardiovascular events (CVEs), the cardiovascular effects of HMPV remain under-characterized. The study aimed to assess the prevalence of pre-existing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and the incidence of acute CVEs in adults with laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection. A PRISMA-guided review of MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar (Jan. 2000–Sept. 2025) identified 18 studies, nine of which were critically appraised. Pre-existing CVD was reported in 10–80% of HMPV-infected patients, with chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease being the most common. Acute CVEs, particularly heart failure exacerbations, occurred in 5–25% of hospitalized patients. Underlying CVD was consistently associated with increased illness severity, including higher ICU admission and mortality rates. Despite these findings, the evidence remains limited and observational, underscoring the need for further research and heightened awareness of HMPV-related cardiovascular complications.

papers.title: Reduced expression of human metapneumovirus matrix protein impacts virus assembly and ribonucleoprotein localization.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes severe respiratory tract infections in all cohorts, particularly in vulnerable groups such as children, older adults, and the immunocompromised. The matrix (M) protein of HMPV, like the M proteins of other members of the order Mononegavirales , is involved in virus assembly and budding. However, other functions of the HMPV M protein have yet to be elucidated. To investigate the various functions of the M protein, we used a peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO) antisense agent designed to block translation of the M gene during infection. Treatment with the PPMO targeted against M mRNA (PPMO M ) led to dose-dependent decreases in M expression, and a 10 μM PPMO M treatment applied at 1 hour post-infection (hpi) led to a >95% reduction in M protein at 24 hpi. Reductions in M expression had a significant impact on virus production and viral titers. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) probes used to detect vRNA showed that a reduction in M led to an increase in inclusion body (IB) count per cell, but a decrease in the average IB volume per cell at 12 and 24 hpi. HMPV-infected cells treated with PPMO M exhibited lower levels of phosphoprotein (P) at the plasma membrane. Importantly, no change in viral ribonucleoprotein movement (vRNP) was observed when the M protein levels were reduced. These studies support a model where the M protein does not facilitate movement, but instead is critical for the transfer to and stable association of vRNPs with the assembly sites at the membrane. IMPORTANCE Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a respiratory pathogen that can cause severe infections in humans, but there are no targeted treatment options for HMPV. To better characterize HMPV, a matrix (M) protein-targeted peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO M ) was designed to control M expression during infection. Inhibition of M expression resulted in infections with reduced viral filaments and less viral RNA at the cell periphery. A reduction in M protein expression did not disrupt the active transport of viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNPs) but did significantly decrease vRNP localization at membranes and increase the number of inclusion bodies within infected cells. Viral titers were significantly reduced when M protein expression was inhibited, and dose-dependent reductions in M protein directly correlated with viral particle production. This study uses a unique tool to characterize the HMPV M protein during infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes severe respiratory tract infections in all cohorts, particularly in vulnerable groups such as children, older adults, and the immunocompromised. The study aimed to better characterize the HMPV M protein during infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO) antisense agent to control M expression during infection. HMPV-infected cells were treated with PPMO M to investigate the various functions of the M protein.
analysis.methods: To investigate the various functions of the M protein, a peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO) antisense agent was used to block translation of the M gene during infection. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) probes were used to detect vRNA and assess the impact of M protein reduction on virus assembly and ribonucleoprotein localization.
analysis.main_results: Treatment with the PPMO targeted against M mRNA (PPMO M) led to dose-dependent decreases in M expression, and a 10 μM PPMO M treatment applied at 1 hour post-infection (hpi) led to a >95% reduction in M protein at 24 hpi. A reduction in M protein expression did not disrupt the active transport of viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNPs) but did significantly decrease vRNP localization at membranes and increase the number of inclusion bodies within infected cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the M protein is critical for the transfer to and stable association of vRNPs with the assembly sites at the membrane, rather than facilitating their movement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the role of the M protein in HMPV infection, which could inform the development of targeted therapies for HMPV.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its use of an antisense agent to block M expression, which may not fully replicate natural infection conditions. The evidence is strong as it directly correlates dose-dependent reductions in M protein with significant decreases in viral titers and changes in vRNP localization.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the matrix (M) protein in human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection. HMPV is a respiratory pathogen that causes severe infections, particularly in vulnerable populations. The research aimed to better understand the M protein's functions during infection. Using a peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO) to block M gene translation, the study observed that reduced M expression significantly impacted virus production and viral titers. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) probes revealed that M reduction increased inclusion body count but decreased average IB volume and vRNP localization at membranes. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that the M protein is critical for the transfer and stable association of vRNPs with membrane assembly sites, rather than facilitating their movement. These results could inform the development of targeted therapies for HMPV. However, the study's use of an antisense agent may not fully replicate natural infection conditions, which limits the generalizability of the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 在所有 队列研究 中引起严重呼吸道感染,特别是在儿童、老年人和免疫功能低下等弱势群体中。该研究旨在更好地表征感染期间的 HMPV M 蛋白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用肽缀合的磷酸二酰胺吗啉寡聚物 (PPMO) 反义剂来控制感染过程中 M 的表达。用 PPMO M 处理 HMPV 感染的细胞,以研究 M 蛋白的各种功能。
elements_zh.methods: 为了研究 M 蛋白的各种功能,使用肽缀合的磷酸二酰胺吗啉寡聚物 (PPMO) 反义剂来阻断感染期间 M 基因的翻译。使用荧光原位杂交 (FISH) 探针检测 vRNA 并评估 M 蛋白减少对病毒组装和核糖核蛋白定位的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 治疗 与针对 M mRNA (PPMO M) 的 PPMO 导致 M 表达呈剂量依赖性下降,感染后 1 小时 (hpi) 应用 10 μM PPMO M 治疗 导致 24 hpi 时 M 蛋白减少 > 95%。M蛋白表达的减少不会破坏病毒核糖核蛋白(vRNP)的主动运输,但会显着降低vRNP在膜上的定位并增加感染细胞内包涵体的数量。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,M 蛋白对于 vRNP 转移到膜上的组装位点并与膜上的组装位点稳定结合至关重要,而不是促进它们的移动。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了关于 M 蛋白在 HMPV 感染中的作用的见解,这可以为 HMPV 靶向治疗的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于使用反义剂来阻断 M 表达,这可能无法完全复制自然感染条件。证据是强有力的,因为它将 M 蛋白的剂量依赖性减少与病毒滴度的显着降低和 vRNP 定位的变化直接相关。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 在所有 队列研究 中引起严重呼吸道感染,特别是在儿童、老年人和免疫功能低下等弱势群体中。该研究旨在更好地表征感染期间的 HMPV M 蛋白。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用肽缀合的磷酸二酰胺吗啉寡聚物 (PPMO) 反义剂来控制感染过程中 M 的表达。用 PPMO M 处理 HMPV 感染的细胞,以研究 M 蛋白的各种功能。
analysis_zh.methods: 为了研究 M 蛋白的各种功能,使用肽缀合的磷酸二酰胺吗啉寡聚物 (PPMO) 反义剂来阻断感染期间 M 基因的翻译。使用荧光原位杂交 (FISH) 探针检测 vRNA 并评估 M 蛋白减少对病毒组装和核糖核蛋白定位的影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: 治疗 与针对 M mRNA (PPMO M) 的 PPMO 导致 M 表达呈剂量依赖性下降,感染后 1 小时 (hpi) 应用 10 μM PPMO M 治疗 导致 24 hpi 时 M 蛋白减少 > 95%。M蛋白表达的减少不会破坏病毒核糖核蛋白(vRNP)的主动运输,但会显着降低vRNP在膜上的定位并增加感染细胞内包涵体的数量。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,M 蛋白对于 vRNP 转移到膜上的组装位点并与膜上的组装位点稳定结合至关重要,而不是促进它们的移动。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了关于 M 蛋白在 HMPV 感染中的作用的见解,这可以为 HMPV 靶向治疗的开发提供信息。

papers.title: Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, RSV, and Human Metapneumovirus Across the COVID-19 Era: An Eight-Year Tertiary-Center Study in Saudi Arabia
papers.abstract: Background: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) caused by viruses are a public health problem, contributing to hospital admissions and morbidity worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered the detection patterns of respiratory viruses through public health interventions. Longitudinal data on these changes and viral seasonality remain limited in Saudi Arabia. This eight-year study evaluated epidemiological and seasonal patterns of major respiratory viruses across the COVID-19 era at a major Saudi tertiary care center. Methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted at King Khalid University Hospital, Riyadh, from October 2017 to December 2025. PCR-confirmed detections for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A, Influenza B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV) were extracted from the hospital Laboratory Information System. Demographics, co-detection, seasonality, and length of stay (LOS) were analyzed across four eras spanning the pre-COVID-19, lockdown, restriction, and post-restriction periods using descriptive statistics, the Kruskal–Wallis test, and multivariable negative binomial regression. Results: Among 5708 confirmed respiratory viral detection episodes, SARS-CoV-2 was the most frequently detected (52.5%), followed by Influenza A (19.1%), RSV (16.4%), Influenza B (8.4%), and HMPV (3.6%). Before the pandemic, Influenza A accounted for the largest proportion of detected episodes (71.1%), with detections clustering particularly during autumn and winter seasons, whereas SARS-CoV-2 accounted for the majority of detected episodes during the lockdown and restriction eras (97.4% and 93.2%). The post-restriction era became more diverse, with RSV being detected in substantial proportions (28.3%), showing prominent winter activity. RSV and HMPV predominantly affected children aged 0–5 years, whereas SARS-CoV-2 was more frequently detected among older adults. Among adults, older age was associated with prolonged LOS; Influenza A and HMPV were associated with shorter stays compared to SARS-CoV-2. Among children, no virus was independently associated with LOS after adjustment for age and sex; however, older age was associated with longer hospital stays. Conclusion: The observed detection patterns of major respiratory viruses shifted substantially across the COVID-19 eras, with notable post-restriction diversification among observed positive detections. LOS was associated with age in both adults and children and with virus type among adults, supporting continued surveillance to guide preventive and clinical strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由病毒引起的呼吸道感染 (RTI) 是一个公共卫生问题,导致全世界住院人数和发病率增加。本研究旨在评估整个 COVID-19 时代主要呼吸道病毒的流行病学和季节性模式。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2017 年 10 月至 2025 年 12 月在利雅得哈立德国王大学医院进行了一项回顾性观察研究。该研究包括对 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感、乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 的 PCR 确认检测。
elements_zh.methods: 从医院实验室信息系统中提取了 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感、乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 的 PCR 确认检测结果。使用描述性统计、Kruskal-Wallis 检验和多变量负二项式回归,对跨越 COVID-19 之前、封锁、限制和限制后四个时期的人口统计、共同检测、季节性和住院时间 (LOS) 进行了分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 5708 例确诊的呼吸道病毒检测事件中,SARS-CoV-2 检测频率最高(52.5%),其次是甲型流感(19.1%)、RSV(16.4%)、乙型流感(8.4%)和 HMPV(3.6%)。RSV 和 HMPV 主要影响 0-5 岁儿童,而 SARS-CoV-2 在老年人中更常见。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在 COVID-19 时代,观察到的主要呼吸道病毒的检测模式发生了很大变化,观察到的阳性检测在限制后出现了显着的多样化。LOS 与成人和儿童的年龄以及成人的病毒类型相关,支持持续的 监测 来指导预防和临床策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了呼吸道病毒检测和住院模式的动态变化,这可以为 人偏肺病毒 和其他呼吸道病毒的针对性 人偏肺病毒 和临床管理策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制建立因果关系的能力。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于没有实验控制的观察数据和统计分析。

analysis_zh.methods: 从医院实验室信息系统中提取了 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感、乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 的 PCR 确认检测结果。使用描述性统计、Kruskal-Wallis 检验和多变量负二项式回归,对跨越 COVID-19 之前、封锁、限制和限制后四个时期的人口统计、共同检测、季节性和住院时间 (LOS) 进行了分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 5708 例确诊的呼吸道病毒检测事件中,SARS-CoV-2 检测频率最高(52.5%),其次是甲型流感(19.1%)、RSV(16.4%)、乙型流感(8.4%)和 HMPV(3.6%)。RSV 和 HMPV 主要影响 0-5 岁儿童,而 SARS-CoV-2 在老年人中更常见。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在 COVID-19 时代,观察到的主要呼吸道病毒的检测模式发生了很大变化,观察到的阳性检测在限制后出现了显着的多样化。LOS 与成人和儿童的年龄以及成人的病毒类型相关,支持持续的 监测 来指导预防和临床策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了呼吸道病毒检测和住院模式的动态变化,这可以为 人偏肺病毒 和其他呼吸道病毒的针对性 人偏肺病毒 和临床管理策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制建立因果关系的能力。证据是中等的,因为它依赖于没有实验控制的观察数据和统计分析。

papers.title: Epidemiological and Molecular Characterization of Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) in Children Under 14 Years of Age in Shijiazhuang City, China
papers.abstract: Objective: The objectives of this study were to analyze the epidemiological characteristics and whole-genome features of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) among children under 14 years of age in Shijiazhuang during 2022–2025, enrich the whole-genome data of HMPV in China, and provide a basis for further understanding the genetic diversity of the virus and for its prevention, control, and transmission intervention. Methods: A total of 1920 cases of acute respiratory infection were enrolled from three sentinel hospitals in Shijiazhuang. Nucleic acid screening was performed using real-time PCR. Whole-genome sequencing was conducted on 25 positive samples. Phylogenetic trees were constructed using the neighbor-joining method in MEGA, and nucleotide and amino acid sequence identity analyses were performed. Results: The overall detection rate of HMPV from 2022 to 2025 was 4.17%. A prominent peak in winter 2024 was the major distinguishing feature. Temporally, both influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases showed marked seasonality during 2022–2025, with high-incidence periods in December–March and April–June. BLAST alignment and phylogenetic analysis showed that among the 25 sequenced HMPV specimens, genotype B2 was the most frequently identified genotype (13/25, 52%). Conclusions: HMPV epidemics in Shijiazhuang during 2022–2025 mainly occurred in winter–spring and spring–summer, with a notable detection peak in December 2024. The B2 genotype predominated among the sequenced HMPV isolates obtained in this study. The amino acid variation in the G gene was significantly higher than that in other genomic regions.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 1920 cases of acute respiratory infection were enrolled from three sentinel hospitals in Shijiazhuang during 2022–2025. The study focused on children under 14 years of age, with nucleic acid screening using real-time PCR and whole-genome sequencing performed on 25 positive samples.
analysis.methods: Nucleic acid screening was performed using real-time PCR to identify HMPV cases. Whole-genome sequencing was conducted on 25 positive samples, and phylogenetic trees were constructed using the neighbor-joining method in MEGA. Nucleotide and amino acid sequence identity analyses were also performed.
analysis.main_results: The overall detection rate of HMPV from 2022 to 2025 was 4.17%. A prominent peak in winter 2024 was the major distinguishing feature. Temporally, both influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases showed marked seasonality during 2022–2025, with high-incidence periods in December–March and April–June. Among the 25 sequenced HMPV specimens, genotype B2 was the most frequently identified genotype (13/25, 52%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified a notable detection peak in December 2024 and highlighted the predominance of genotype B2 among the sequenced HMPV isolates. It also noted that amino acid variation in the G gene was significantly higher than that in other genomic regions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the seasonal patterns and genetic diversity of HMPV in Shijiazhuang, which can inform surveillance strategies, diagnosis, and the development of targeted prevention and control measures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on sentinel hospitals, which may not represent the entire population. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on a specific geographic and temporal context, and the sample size for sequencing is relatively small.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the epidemiological and molecular characteristics of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) in children under 14 years of age in Shijiazhuang City, China, from 2022 to 2025. The research aimed to enrich HMPV whole-genome data in China and understand its genetic diversity for prevention and control. A total of 1920 acute respiratory infection cases were analyzed, with 25 positive samples undergoing whole-genome sequencing. The overall detection rate was 4.17%, with a significant peak in winter 2024. Seasonal patterns were observed, with high incidence in December–March and April–June. Genotype B2 was the most common among the sequenced isolates, accounting for 52% of cases. The G gene showed higher amino acid variation compared to other genomic regions. The study highlights the importance of monitoring HMPV seasonality and genetic diversity for public health interventions. However, the findings are based on a limited geographic and temporal scope, and the sample size for sequencing is relatively small, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

papers.title_zh: 中国石家庄市 14 岁以下儿童 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 的流行病学和分子特征
papers.source_body_en: Objective: The objectives of this study were to analyze the epidemiological characteristics and whole-genome features of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) among children under 14 years of age in Shijiazhuang during 2022–2025, enrich the whole-genome data of HMPV in China, and provide a basis for further understanding the genetic diversity of the virus and for its prevention, control, and transmission intervention. Methods: A total of 1920 cases of acute respiratory infection were enrolled from three sentinel hospitals in Shijiazhuang. Nucleic acid screening was performed using real-time PCR. Whole-genome sequencing was conducted on 25 positive samples. Phylogenetic trees were constructed using the neighbor-joining method in MEGA, and nucleotide and amino acid sequence identity analyses were performed. Results: The overall detection rate of HMPV from 2022 to 2025 was 4.17%. A prominent peak in winter 2024 was the major distinguishing feature. Temporally, both influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases showed marked seasonality during 2022–2025, with high-incidence periods in December–March and April–June. BLAST alignment and phylogenetic analysis showed that among the 25 sequenced HMPV specimens, genotype B2 was the most frequently identified genotype (13/25, 52%). Conclusions: HMPV epidemics in Shijiazhuang during 2022–2025 mainly occurred in winter–spring and spring–summer, with a notable detection peak in December 2024. The B2 genotype predominated among the sequenced HMPV isolates obtained in this study. The amino acid variation in the G gene was significantly higher than that in other genomic regions.

papers.title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
papers.abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人偏肺病毒 主要针对呼吸道上皮,触发 免疫应答,从而有助于病毒清除和疾病 发病机制。包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂在内的研究疗法显示出希望,但需要进一步验证。免疫调节剂和草药可能会提供支持性益处,但它们对抗 HMPV 的功效尚未得到证实。疫苗 的开发正在进行中,有几个候选药物处于临床前和早期临床阶段。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该病毒通过多种机制逃避 免疫应答,导致疾病严重化,特别是在弱势群体中。尽管目前支持性护理是主流,但新兴的 抗病毒药物 和 疫苗 可能会提供未来的解决方案。改善诊断途径、公众意识和有针对性的研究对于控制 HMPV 感染至关重要。需要进一步的临床试验来建立安全有效的治疗方案。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection and disease. The review focuses on the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and management of HMPV-associated respiratory infections, particularly in vulnerable populations such as young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on HMPV infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Human metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against HMPV remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management.

papers.title_zh: 发病机制、诊断 和 人偏肺病毒 相关呼吸道感染管理的新趋势
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

papers.title: Repositioning antiviral phytoconstituents as broad-spectrum inhibitors of influenza A neuraminidase and human metapneumovirus fusion protein
papers.abstract: Viral respiratory infections still exist as a major global health concern. Influenza A viruses and human metapneumoviruses are among the main pathogens responsible for infections that can progress to severe acute respiratory forms. Despite the availability of certain therapeutic options, the need for effective treatment remains an issue. The exploration of innovative approaches based on medicinal plants, capable of simultaneously targeting several viruses, represents a promising strategic option for limiting the viral activity of these pathogens. In this work, an integrated computational workflow combining molecular docking, ADMET prediction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and MM-PBSA binding free-energy analysis was applied to evaluate previously reported antiviral phytoconstituents for their broad-spectrum antiviral potential by simultaneously targeting influenza A virus neuraminidase (NA) (PDB ID: 2HT7) and the human metapneumovirus (HMPV) fusion protein (F) (PDB ID: 7SEJ). Molecular docking analyses identified 37 phytoconstituents with favorable multi-target binding affinities toward both NA and F proteins, exhibiting more favorable predicted binding energies than the reference compounds oseltamivir and ribavirin. In addition, ADMET prediction, including bioavailability assessment and analysis of pharmacokinetic and toxicological properties, identified several compounds with favorable profiles, notably compounds E10, M294, M329, C11, C5, and M274. MD simulations followed by MM-PBSA binding free-energy calculations further validated the stability and binding behavior of the highest-ranked protein–ligand complexes identified through the sequential screening workflow. Overall, compounds M294 and C11 emerged as the most promising broad-spectrum antiviral lead candidates against both influenza A NA and HMPV F protein. Nevertheless, these findings are based on computational predictions and require confirmation through in vitro antiviral assays followed by in vivo studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of antiviral phytoconstituents as broad-spectrum inhibitors targeting both influenza A neuraminidase and human metapneumovirus fusion protein. Using a computational workflow that includes molecular docking, ADMET prediction, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-PBSA binding free-energy analysis, the researchers identified 37 phytoconstituents with favorable binding affinities toward both viral targets. Among these, compounds M294 and C11 were highlighted as the most promising candidates. The study emphasizes the need for further experimental validation through in vitro and in vivo studies to confirm these computational findings. The results suggest that such compounds could offer a novel therapeutic approach for combating multiple respiratory viruses, potentially reducing the need for separate treatments. However, the study's reliance on computational models limits the strength of the evidence, highlighting the importance of experimental verification.

papers.title_zh: 将 抗病毒药物 植物成分重新定位为甲型流感神经氨酸酶和 人偏肺病毒 融合蛋白的广谱抑制剂
papers.source_body_en: Viral respiratory infections still exist as a major global health concern. Influenza A viruses and human metapneumoviruses are among the main pathogens responsible for infections that can progress to severe acute respiratory forms. Despite the availability of certain therapeutic options, the need for effective treatment remains an issue. The exploration of innovative approaches based on medicinal plants, capable of simultaneously targeting several viruses, represents a promising strategic option for limiting the viral activity of these pathogens. In this work, an integrated computational workflow combining molecular docking, ADMET prediction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and MM-PBSA binding free-energy analysis was applied to evaluate previously reported antiviral phytoconstituents for their broad-spectrum antiviral potential by simultaneously targeting influenza A virus neuraminidase (NA) (PDB ID: 2HT7) and the human metapneumovirus (HMPV) fusion protein (F) (PDB ID: 7SEJ). Molecular docking analyses identified 37 phytoconstituents with favorable multi-target binding affinities toward both NA and F proteins, exhibiting more favorable predicted binding energies than the reference compounds oseltamivir and ribavirin. In addition, ADMET prediction, including bioavailability assessment and analysis of pharmacokinetic and toxicological properties, identified several compounds with favorable profiles, notably compounds E10, M294, M329, C11, C5, and M274. MD simulations followed by MM-PBSA binding free-energy calculations further validated the stability and binding behavior of the highest-ranked protein–ligand complexes identified through the sequential screening workflow. Overall, compounds M294 and C11 emerged as the most promising broad-spectrum antiviral lead candidates against both influenza A NA and HMPV F protein. Nevertheless, these findings are based on computational predictions and require confirmation through in vitro antiviral assays followed by in vivo studies.

papers.title: Clinical and Analytical Validation of a Novel Switching RT-qPCR Assay for the Simultaneous Detection of Seven Respiratory Viruses.
papers.abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of respiratory viruses is essential for effective clinical management and infection control. However, conventional RT-qPCR methods are time-consuming and require complex workflows. To address these limitations, we developed a novel Switching RT-qPCR assay designed for multiplex detection of respiratory viruses with enhanced efficiency and sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical and clinical performance of the switching RT-qPCR assay in the detection of seven major respiratory viruses: Influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, adenovirus (AdV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and SARS-CoV-2 (Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2). Nasopharyngeal swab specimens (n = 808) were collected from patients with respiratory symptoms. RNA was extracted and tested using both a Switching RT-qPCR assay and commercial multiplex RT-qPCR method (Allplex Respiratory Panels and Allplex SARS-CoV-2 Assay). The concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and analytical performances of the two methods were compared. The Switching RT-qPCR assay demonstrated a clinical sensitivity of 93.6% and a specificity of 100%, with an overall concordance rate exceeding 96%, compared with the conventional assay. Analytical sensitivity was comparable or superior across most viral targets, particularly RSV A, AdV, and hMPV. The duplex assay format enabled the efficient simultaneous detection of two targets per reaction, reducing the overall testing time while maintaining analytical accuracy. This Switching RT-qPCR assay offers a reliable, rapid, and efficient alternative for respiratory virus detection. Its simplified duplex format and high concordance with standard molecular diagnostics indicate its potential utility in routine clinical laboratories.

papers.title_zh: 用于同时检测七种呼吸道病毒的新型转换 RT-qPCR 测定的临床和分析验证。
papers.source_body_en: Rapid and accurate identification of respiratory viruses is essential for effective clinical management and infection control. However, conventional RT-qPCR methods are time-consuming and require complex workflows. To address these limitations, we developed a novel Switching RT-qPCR assay designed for multiplex detection of respiratory viruses with enhanced efficiency and sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical and clinical performance of the switching RT-qPCR assay in the detection of seven major respiratory viruses: Influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, adenovirus (AdV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and SARS-CoV-2 (Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2). Nasopharyngeal swab specimens (n = 808) were collected from patients with respiratory symptoms. RNA was extracted and tested using both a Switching RT-qPCR assay and commercial multiplex RT-qPCR method (Allplex Respiratory Panels and Allplex SARS-CoV-2 Assay). The concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and analytical performances of the two methods were compared. The Switching RT-qPCR assay demonstrated a clinical sensitivity of 93.6% and a specificity of 100%, with an overall concordance rate exceeding 96%, compared with the conventional assay. Analytical sensitivity was comparable or superior across most viral targets, particularly RSV A, AdV, and hMPV. The duplex assay format enabled the efficient simultaneous detection of two targets per reaction, reducing the overall testing time while maintaining analytical accuracy. This Switching RT-qPCR assay offers a reliable, rapid, and efficient alternative for respiratory virus detection. Its simplified duplex format and high concordance with standard molecular diagnostics indicate its potential utility in routine clinical laboratories.
papers.abstract_zh: 快速、准确地识别呼吸道病毒对于有效的临床管理和感染控制至关重要。然而,传统的 RT-qPCR 方法非常耗时且需要复杂的工作流程。为了解决这些限制,我们开发了一种新型开关 RT-qPCR 检测方法,旨在提高呼吸道病毒的多重检测效率和灵敏度。本研究旨在评估转换 RT-qPCR 检测在检测七种主要呼吸道病毒时的分析和临床性能:甲型和乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) A 和 B、腺病毒 (AdV)、人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 和 SARS-CoV-2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2)。鼻咽拭子标本(n = 808)是从有呼吸道症状的患者身上采集的。使用 Switching RT-qPCR 测定和商业多重 RT-qPCR 方法(Allplex Respiratory Panels 和 Allplex SARS-CoV-2 Assay)提取和测试 RNA。比较了两种方法的一致性、灵敏度、特异性和分析性能。与传统检测相比,Switching RT-qPCR 检测的临床敏感性为 93.6%,特异性为 100%,总体一致性率超过 96%。大多数病毒靶标(尤其是 RSV A、AdV 和 hMPV)的分析灵敏度相当或更高。双工检测形式能够在每个反应中同时有效检测两个目标,从而减少总体测试时间,同时保持分析准确性。这种转换 RT-qPCR 检测为呼吸道病毒检测提供了可靠、快速且高效的替代方案。其简化的双工形式以及与标准分子诊断的高度一致性表明其在常规临床实验室中的潜在实用性。

papers.title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram for Predicting Severe Respiratory Illness in Children with Isolated Human Metapneumovirus Infection
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory tract infections in children, but comorbidities and mixed infections have confounded most previous studies. This study aimed to develop an early prediction model for severe respiratory illness in children with isolated hMPV infection. Methods: This retrospective study enrolled 540 children with isolated hMPV infection (without comorbidities or mixed infections) hospitalised between February 2022 and January 2024. Severe respiratory illness was defined according to British Thoracic Society guidelines. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify predictors and develop a nomogram, with model performance evaluated by AUC, Hosmer–Lemeshow test, and bootstrap validation. Results: Six independent predictors were identified: male sex (protective factor, OR = 0.500), elevated neutrophil count (OR = 1.114), decreased lymphocyte count (OR = 0.829), decreased prealbumin level (OR = 0.992), crackles (OR = 1.858), and wheezes (OR = 3.734). The nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.743 (95% CI: 0.690–0.796) and demonstrated good calibration performance (Hosmer–Lemeshow p = 0.139, Brier score = 0.136). Risk stratification classified patients into low-risk ( 30%) groups, with severe illness rates of 5.1%, 16.7%, and 46.0%, respectively (p < 0.001). Conclusions: The nomogram incorporating six early-admission indicators may serve as a practical tool for early risk stratification in hospitalised children with isolated hMPV infection.

papers.title: Clinician-Reported Respiratory Viral Testing and Intended Management of Community-Acquired Respiratory Viral Infections in Haematology and Haematopoietic Cell Transplantation: An International Exploratory Survey
papers.abstract: Background: Community-acquired respiratory viruses (CARVs) cause significant morbidity and mortality in patients with haematological malignancies and those undergoing haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Despite this, clinical management remains variable. This study evaluated clinicians’ awareness, diagnostic practices, and treatment approaches to major respiratory viruses in this high-risk population. Methods: An international electronic survey using non-probability convenience sampling was conducted among haematology, oncology, intensive care and emergency medicine physicians. Four real-life clinical cases were converted into standardised vignettes covering human metapneumovirus (HMPV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) and influenza A virus (IAV). The questionnaire assessed reported testing strategies and intended management, including antiviral and immunoprophylactic interventions. Responses were analysed descriptively; no inferential between-group comparisons were performed. Results: Ninety-eight clinicians from 26 countries responded. Diagnostic approaches, including testing indications and panel selection, varied among respondents. For HMPV and HPIV, respondents mainly reported supportive care, immunoglobulin replacement, and infection-control measures in the absence of established pathogen-specific interventions. RSV practice was heterogeneous: systemic ribavirin was considered by 45/96 (46.9%) respondents, including 34/96 (35.4%) when guided by an immunodeficiency score. IAV management was more consistent, with reported availability of vaccination and antiviral therapy and frequent use of post-exposure prophylaxis. Conclusions: Within this international convenience sample, clinicians reported variation in respiratory viral testing and in how results informed intended management. Because sampling was non-probability-based and respondent groups were small and unevenly distributed, the findings should not be interpreted as representative estimates of international practice. IAV testing was most consistently linked to established treatment and prevention, RSV showed greater therapeutic and preventive heterogeneity, and HMPV/HPIV testing primarily informed infection control, monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores clinician-reported practices in respiratory viral testing and management for human metapneumovirus (HMPV) in high-risk populations, such as patients with haematological malignancies and those undergoing haematopoietic cell transplantation. The research highlights significant variability in diagnostic approaches and treatment strategies, particularly for HMPV and HPIV, where no established interventions exist. The study used an international electronic survey with non-probability convenience sampling, collecting responses from 98 clinicians across 26 countries. It found that HMPV and HPIV testing primarily informed infection control, monitoring, and antimicrobial stewardship, while IAV testing was more consistent with available treatments and prevention strategies. RSV management showed greater heterogeneity, with some clinicians considering systemic ribavirin. The authors caution that the findings are not representative due to the non-probability sampling and uneven distribution of respondents. The study contributes to understanding current practices and underscores the need for standardised approaches in managing respiratory viral infections in immunocompromised patients.

papers.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Respiratory Viral Infections in Pediatric Cancer Patients, Single center experience
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory viral (RV) infections cause morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised pediatric patients undergoing cancer treatment. The burden of RV infections in pediatric oncology populations from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain limited. We aimed to detect the prevalence of viruses causing respiratory infections among pediatric patients with cancer and guide empiric therapy and improve patient outcomes. Methods Retrospectively we collected nasopharyngeal swabs and clinical and demographic data from pediatric patients under cancer treatment with respiratory symptoms at Children’s Cancer Hospital Egypt-57357 from September 2023 until March 2025. Samples were tested using multiplex PCR for 16 respiratory viruses. Results A total of 1710 samples were collected from 784 patients with a median age of 7 years and a male-to-female ratio of 1.26:1. Viral pathogens were detected in 1037 swabs (60.6%). The most frequently identified virus was human rhinovirus (HRV) (51.3%), followed by parainfluenza virus (PIV) (9%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (8%), SARS-CoV-2 (6.4%), and human metapneumovirus (HmpV) (5.8%). papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道病毒 (RV) 感染会导致患有癌症 治疗 的免疫功能低下儿科患者发病和 死亡率。低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 儿童肿瘤人群的 RV 感染负担仍然有限。我们的目的是检测引起儿科癌症患者呼吸道感染的病毒的 患病率,并指导经验性治疗和改善患者的治疗结果。方法 回顾性收集了 2023 年 9 月至 2025 年 3 月在埃及 57357 儿童癌症医院出现呼吸道症状的 治疗 癌症儿童患者的鼻咽拭子以及临床和人口统计数据。使用多重 PCR 对样本进行了 16 种呼吸道病毒检测。结果共收集784例患者1710份样本,中位年龄7岁,男女比例1.26:1。在 1037 份拭子(60.6%)中检测到病毒病原体。最常见的病毒是人鼻病毒 (HRV) (51.3%),其次是副流感病毒 (PIV) (9%)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) (8%)、SARS-CoV-2 (6.4%) 和 人偏肺病毒 (HmpV) (5.8%)。13% 的样本中观察到混合感染,通常涉及 RSV、PIV 和腺病毒。主要症状为发热(85.7%)、下呼吸道感染(LRTI)(59.4%)和咳嗽(57.7%)。HRV 与发烧 (p=0.01)、咳嗽 (p=0.02) 和入院 (p=0.006) 相关。PIV 感染与入院率增加 (p=0.04) 和正性肌力药物需求增加 (p=0.02) 相关,而 HmpV 与 LRTI 显着相关 (p=0.01)。病毒类型和 死亡率 之间没有统计学上的显着关联 (p=0.64)。当将患者特征与临床症状和结果关联起来时,发现了一些显着的关联。中性粒细胞计数较低(<500)与鼻漏(p<0.001)、需氧量(p=0.01)、入院(p=0.001)和入院重症监护病房(p=0.04)相关。女性性别与需氧量 (p=0.03) 和入住 ICU (p=0.02) 显着相关;患有血液系统恶性肿瘤的患者更有可能需要氧气支持(p=0.01)。结论 RV 感染在有呼吸道症状的儿童癌症患者中很常见,以 HRV 为主,且与关键临床表现和入院情况相关。宿主 因素(例如女性、血液肿瘤和严重中性粒细胞减少症)也与疾病严重程度增加和支持性护理需求增加相关。然而,死亡率 在病毒类型之间没有显着差异,这表明虽然 RV 感染对发病率有很大影响,但免疫功能低下儿童的 死亡率 可能取决于多因素 宿主 和疾病相关因素。

papers.title: Post-pandemic ecological reshaping of respiratory pathogen circulation: A six-year FilmArray(R)-based surveillance study in Tokyo, Japan (2020-2026)
papers.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered respiratory pathogen circulation worldwide. However, longitudinal analyses of changes in respiratory pathogen ecology across the pandemic and post-pandemic periods remain limited. Methods We analyzed 19,968 respiratory samples tested with the BioFire(R) FilmArray(R) Respiratory Panel at a hospital in Tokyo, Japan, between January 2020 and March 2026. We evaluated temporal changes in pathogen circulation, age-specific epidemiology, co-detection patterns, pairwise pathogen associations, and clinical parameters. Results At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 27.8% of tests. Respiratory pathogens resurged asynchronously following the relaxation of COVID-19-related public health measures. Influenza virus circulation remained markedly suppressed until late 2022 before re-emerging in successive large seasonal epidemics, whereas other pathogens, including RSV, human metapneumovirus, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae, exhibited distinct resurgence patterns. Pathogen distributions also varied by age. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus remained predominant among young children, whereas SARS-CoV-2 predominated among older adults. Co-detection occurred in 14.0% of positive specimens and was significantly more frequent in younger patients. Pairwise analysis identified both positive and negative pathogen associations; however, the patterns varied across age groups and study periods. Conclusions Respiratory pathogen circulation changed substantially during the transition from the COVID-19 pandemic to the post-pandemic period, with pathogen-specific, age- and period-dependent patterns. Continued surveillance is warranted to determine how respiratory pathogen circulation will evolve and to inform infection control strategies in the post-pandemic era.

The study highlights the need for continued surveillance to inform infection control strategies. However, the findings are limited by the study's reliance on a single hospital's data and the general nature of the conclusions.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 COVID-19 大流行极大地改变了全球呼吸道病原体的传播。然而,对大流行期间和大流行后时期呼吸道病原体生态变化的纵向分析仍然有限。方法 我们分析了 2020 年 1 月至 2026 年 3 月期间在日本东京一家医院使用 BioFire(R) FilmArray(R) 呼吸面板测试的 19,968 个呼吸道样本。我们评估了病原体循环的时间变化、年龄特异性 流行病学、共同检测模式、成对病原体关联和临床参数。结果 27.8% 的检测中至少检测到一种呼吸道病原体。随着 COVID-19 相关公共卫生措施的放松,呼吸道病原体异步复苏。直到 2022 年底,流感病毒的传播一直受到明显抑制,然后在连续的大规模季节性流行中重新出现,而其他病原体,包括 RSV、人偏肺病毒 和肺炎支原体,则表现出明显的复苏模式。病原体分布也因年龄而异。人鼻病毒/肠道病毒在幼儿中仍然占主导地位,而 SARS-CoV-2 在老年人中占主导地位。14.0% 的阳性样本中出现了共同检测,并且在年轻患者中出现的频率明显更高。配对分析确定了阳性和阴性病原体关联;然而,不同年龄组和学习时期的模式有所不同。结论 在从 COVID-19 大流行到大流行后时期的过渡期间,呼吸道病原体循环发生了巨大变化,具有病原体特异性、年龄和时期依赖性模式。持续的 监测 有必要确定呼吸道病原体循环将如何演变,并为大流行后时代的感染控制策略提供信息。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查大流行后时期如何影响呼吸道病原体循环,特别关注在放松与COVID-19大流行相关的公共卫生措施后人偏肺病毒(hMPV)和其他呼吸道病原体的生态重塑。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项为期六年的 监测 研究,在日本东京的一家医院进行,使用 BioFire(R) FilmArray(R) 呼吸面板分析 2020 年 1 月至 2026 年 3 月期间收集的 19,968 个呼吸道样本。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用 BioFire(R) FilmArray(R) 呼吸面板测试呼吸道样本,并评估病原体循环、特定年龄 流行病学、共同检测模式、成对病原体关联和临床参数的时间变化。
analysis_zh.main_results: 27.8% 的检测中至少检测到一种呼吸道病原体,人偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 循环一直受到明显抑制,直到 2022 年底才在连续的大规模季节性流行病中重新出现。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,从大流行到大流行后时期的过渡期间,呼吸道病原体循环发生了很大变化,观察到了病原体特异性、年龄和时期依赖性模式。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,持续的 监测 对于了解呼吸道病原体循环将如何演变并为大流行后时代的感染控制策略提供信息是必要的。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于单个医院的数据,这些数据可能无法代表更广泛的人群,而且从观察到的模式得出的结论的一般性质。
